clue.text: Most energetic person in Britain, it's Brown usually

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person bursting with energy, the liveliest in any group
second meaning: in British mains wiring the conductor carrying current is coloured brown

explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Brown look like Gordon Brown the politician, but it is the colour of a cable in a British plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A person full of vitality is idiomatically called this, and the same term names the current-carrying cable in household electrics.

clue.text: Star is vain, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for vain is to be taken as spoken, giving a word with the same sound but different spelling

parts.note: vain, as in useless or futile, means idle (idle threats)

explanation.surface: A celebrity is said to be conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: A star of film or pop is an object of fan worship, a synonym in the celebrity sense.

clue.text: Clingy sort, lady primarily this writer's indulged

indicators.note: primarily means at the start, so only the opening letter of lady is used

parts.note: the setter referring to themself: this writer is = I'm
an indulged child or favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: A needy lady confesses the writer has spoiled her.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish grips rocks tightly, so a person who clings to others is figuratively called one.

clue.text: Extremely interesting old coin that's worthless

indicators.note: the extremes of interesting are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: the noble was a medieval English gold coin

explanation.surface: An antique coin may be fascinating but has no value.
explanation.definitionFit: Base or dishonourable, with no merit, which is a loose synonym of lacking worth in character.

clue.text: Country clearing mum seen to support outlaw

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below the first and so hold it up

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a clearing in a wood is a glade
mum, as in keep quiet, is the hush word sh

explanation.surface: A mother seems to back a fugitive while clearing out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: A South Asian nation on the Bay of Bengal, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Some misspelt subtitles put up in haste

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run lying inside it

explanation.surface: Subtitles full of spelling errors were posted in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'misspelt subtitles' runs ELTSUB; 'put up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy, hurried activity; to rush about is to show haste, so the noun is a near synonym.

clue.text: Twigs maybe Billie Jean keeps Nadal fit regularly

indicators.note: keeps means the surname holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Billie Jean King, the American tennis champion

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of Nadal fit is taken

explanation.surface: One tennis great keeps another in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a word about fitness but only supplies a letter to the regular selection running across 'Nadal fit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dry sticks are used to start a fire; twigs are an example of such material, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Tablet's good, no question, for dog

indicators.note: good, no question means the letter for good is used where the question letter stood

parts.note: a plaque is a commemorative tablet on a wall

explanation.surface: A pill is apparently fine for a pet, beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to pursue or trouble persistently, not the animal the tablet seems meant for.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass or torment continually; troubles that pursue someone are said to follow and bother them.

clue.text: Creature European roughly treated at first

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of treated is used

explanation.surface: An animal was handled harshly by a foreigner at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a dark brown carnivore related to the weasel, an instance of a creature.

clue.text: Failing to start standard treatment

indicators.note: the word for standard fails to start, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: an ideal is a standard to aim for

explanation.surface: A therapy that didn't begin properly.
explanation.definitionFit: How one is treated, as in a raw deal or a fair deal: the word means treatment received.

clue.text: Tape of girl performing in Don Juan

indicators.note: letters performing are made to act differently, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A recording of a young woman singing in Mozart's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Mozart's Don Giovanni; here Don Juan is a womaniser and the answer is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer, so a wastrel and libertine, a dissolute person; the noun sense of the answer.

clue.text: Trophy fool rejected previously as paltry

indicators.note: previously means this piece comes before the next one
rejected means sent back, so the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: a nit, or nitwit, is a fool
a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: Someone stupid had earlier turned down an award as too small.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty and of little worth, as in a tinpot dictator; a near synonym for insignificant.

clue.text: Gosh, a party organised for polymath!

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight that a celebration was arranged for a learned person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker worked in mathematics, philosophy, music and mysticism, so an example of a many-sided scholar.

clue.text: Salt in Spooner's food recently

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first consonants of the two words change places

parts.note: tack is food, as in hardtack, a ship's biscuit
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: Adding salt to a meal lately, says the reverend.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of TACK LATE and you hear LACK TATE, spelt as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a salt or ester of lactic acid; the noun sense, not the verb about milk.

clue.text: Labour MP perhaps that's quit is malcontent ultimately

parts.note: quit, past tense, means left

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of malcontent

explanation.surface: A disgruntled MP has finally resigned from the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist or progressive; a Labour member is typically one, so an example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Disgraceful thing, boys raised to eat little peeled

indicators.note: to eat means to take another piece inside
in a down clue raised means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: lads are boys

indicators.note: peeled means the outer letters, like skin, are removed

parts.note: scant means little or barely enough

explanation.surface: Boys brought up on a meagre peeled diet makes for shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' here is an adjective meaning barely enough, and peeling it strips its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage or disgrace causing public shock; a direct synonym in noun form.

clue.text: Play board game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice
second meaning: the black-and-white disc game, also called reversi

explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction to play a board game, the clue is really two names.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a Shakespeare tragedy and a commercial two-player strategy game of flipping counters.

clue.text: Refuse student daughter sufficient amount to purchase article

indicators.note: purchase also means a grip or hold, so these letters grip the article inside

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's L-plate
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter
one's fill is a sufficient amount
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A student turns down having the daughter buy enough of an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A site where rubbish is buried; the waste dumped there, by metonymy, means garbage.

clue.text: Male stops right cheat transforming return contest

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so it goes inside the other letters
transforming means the letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man halts a fraud and it becomes a fresh competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A second game between the same opponents; a replay or return fixture.

clue.text: Issue revolutionary pamphlet an American collects

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards
the phrase collects the letters within it, hiding them across the words

explanation.surface: A subversive tract that a US citizen gathers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to describe the pamphlet; it signals turning the hidden letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or proceed from a source, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Number emerging from taxi expressing thanks

definitions.text: Number emerging from taxi expressing thanks

parts.words: Number emerging from taxi expressing thanks
parts.note: split the word for a cab as an informal thank-you followed by a Roman numeral; what is left after the thanks is the number

explanation.walkthrough: TAXI is TA (British slang for thanks) plus XI, the Roman numeral for this number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral XI stands for the count one more than ten, and also names a cricket or football side.

clue.text: Responsible for tie retired ambassador is wearing

indicators.note: is wearing means the outer word has the other piece on inside it

parts.note: to tie is to bind

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat who has stepped down sports a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: To be behind a plan is to be its instigator, the one accountable for it.

clue.text: Invited Democrat visits top man in Washington

indicators.note: visits means goes into, so this letter is placed inside the name

parts.note: Joe Biden, US president when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A party member calls on the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of bid, in the sense ask to come, as in bidden to the feast.

clue.text: Assist worker indirectly

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back or assist it
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Help an employee in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing news at second hand means getting it not directly but through someone else.

clue.text: Politically moderate newspaper, as has been stated before

indicators.note: before means this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: so means thus, as stated, as in 'I told you so'
the FT, the Financial Times, is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A centrist paper, as already said earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft left or soft Tory is a less extreme wing of a party, so mild in politics.

clue.text: Tailor leaves wife for clairvoyant

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: a tailor is one who sews, a sewer

explanation.surface: A dressmaker abandons his spouse for a fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet who sees the future, a near synonym for one with second sight.

clue.text: Memory of everybody on sports field

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public sports field
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A recollection of the whole team out on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Total recall is perfect remembering, so the noun means the faculty of remembering.

clue.text: Sunak's minister with Conservative ally occasionally outside bar

indicators.note: outside means these letters go round the other piece
occasionally means only some, every other letter, of ally are used

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise something

explanation.surface: A Tory colleague of the prime minister partly surrounds a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: James Cleverly served as Foreign and then Home Secretary under Prime Minister Rishi Sunak.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cleverly was a Cabinet member in Rishi Sunak's government, so the surname names that politician.
